issues.description: The problem statement first instructs that SealSaloon should have a final Stock field initialized in the constructor, but later explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static and that related methods be static. Initializing a static (or static final) field in an instance constructor is contradictory and will confuse students whether stock should be instance-level (final) and constructed in the constructor or a shared static field. The solution implements stock as a static final field initialized at declaration, while the problem text suggests constructor initialization—this mismatch can block students or lead to incorrect implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify and align the specification: state that 'stock' is a shared static (preferably 'private static final Stock stock') and should be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer. Remove or reword the instruction that implies initializing the stock in the instance constructor so students are not led to create a non-static field initialized in the constructor.

issues.description: The problem UML and solution use a Stock method named emptyStock(), but the provided template Stock implementation defines clearInventory() instead (different method name). This method-name/signature inconsistency between the problem description and template code will confuse students about which method to use/implement and may cause compilation or testing issues.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Either rename the template's clearInventory() to emptyStock(), or update the problem statement and the solution to refer to clearInventory(). If both names should be supported, add an emptyStock() wrapper in the template that calls clearInventory() (or vice versa) and document the canonical name in the problem text.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) requires a Stock.emptyStock() method, and the solution implements emptyStock(), but the template Stock class provides a method named clearInventory() instead. This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual operation (clearing the stock) creates a mapping burden: students reading the specification will look for emptyStock but only find clearInventory in the template, possibly causing confusion or incorrect implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() (or add an emptyStock() wrapper that calls clearInventory()) so the template, problem statement, and solution use the same identifier for clearing the stock.
